text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: P1 - routing/cache namespace drift impacting variant selection in eu-west-1. Pager: @alice.m, @ben_oncall. Please acknowledge and join #incidents.

alice.m: acked. Joining. I see alerts: 502 spike + model mismatch traces. Opening timeline.

ben_oncall: on my way. Any customer reports yet?

support-bot: Customer alert: 2 customers reported low-quality completions and unexpected behavior; request ids: req_72a, req_87f.

carla_sre: quick snapshot: routing service started returning model variant "gptx-4-mini-quant" for requests pinned to "gptx-4-prod" in eu-west-1. KV cache keys include region+model tag; looks like a namespace collision after recent rollout.

dmitri: pulling logs for kv-store:
```
2026-03-15T02:10:12Z kv_get key="prefix:euw:gptx-4-prod:cache_v2:token-..." -> MISS
2026-03-15T02:10:12Z kv_get key="prefix:unknown:gptx-4-mini-quant:cache_v2:token-..." -> HIT
```
pattern: some upstream routing policy dropped region tag and used fallback namespace 'unknown' which maps to mini-variant cache entries.

alice.m: hypothesis: new smart-routing policy change (deployed 02:00Z) changed tag order for keys; when fallback logic runs it constructs cache_key without canonical region leading to reuse of wrong cached KV for different variant. That would cause logits/kv reuse across variants.

ben_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) stop smart-routing rollout (revert canary), 2) disable KV-prefetch caching for euw region temporarily, 3) add a reject rule for mismatched variant cache hits. Who can hit the revert?

ops-lead: I'm on revert. Rolling back routing policy to previous commit now.

carla_sre: while ops reverts, I can flip the cache gate on the runtime group. Command (run on control plane):
```
POST /admin/flags/cache_prefixing
{"region":"eu-west-1","enabled":false}
```
I'll apply in 30s after revert low-risk window.

dmitri: collecting metrics: affected QPS ~ 120 r/s, error-rate elevated +9%, customer latency unchanged. Customer-impact estimate: ~0.6% of requests in euw producing incorrect completions (based on sampling).

support-bot: Notifying CSMs and creating interim incident notice to impacted customers. Draft note: "We're investigating incorrect model outputs in EU — mitigation in progress, will follow up." @customer-success please review.

customer-success: seen, sending to customers with sensitive contexts flagged. Requesting ETA for full rollback.

ops-lead: revert submitted (deploy id deploy-20260315-0218), status: in-progress -> success.

alice.m: revert confirmed. Smart-routing policy back to v1.2.4. Now toggling cache flag.

carla_sre: cache_prefixing disabled in eu-west-1. Monitoring for reduction in mismatched variant serve. Also added temporary reject-rule:
```
iptables-like rule: if cache.namespace.variant != request.variant -> reject_cache_hit
```

dmitri: sampling shows mismatch drops to near-zero within two minutes. Error-rate falling back to baseline. Customer incorrect completions count stops increasing.

ben_oncall: running sanity checks: running batch eval on pinned prompts for affected customers. Initial quality metrics restored for 98% of samples.

customer-success: sending update to customers: mitigation applied, we are rolling back config change and will perform root cause postmortem. Response looks positive so far.

alice.m: next steps: 1) production postmortem scheduled (owner: carla_sre), 2) revert changelog and add strict unit tests for cache-key generation (include region+variant order), 3) add e2e sim test to routing CI to surface namespace drift.

carla_sre: created incident doc and postmortem stub. Action items assigned. I'll also add alert rule for variant mismatch ratio >0.1%.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident marked as mitigated. Status: customer-impacting, P1 -> mitigated. Please update the timeline in the incident doc and add any additional context. Closing pager wave.

ops-lead: leaving final note: root cause appears to be ordering change in routing policy's tag normalization logic introduced in canary. Fix: enforce canonical tag ordering and tighten cache key factory to be deterministic across rollouts. I'll followup with a CR to the routing service.

alice.m: thanks team. Handoff to postmortem owners. I'll remain as on-call follow-up for 1h in case any regressions pop up. :thumbsup:

support-bot: All done. Incident channel unlocked for normal traffic.
